newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends marginally weaker at 26.285.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends marginally weaker at 26.285.

text.p: * Central Bank prevents peso from falling

The Philippine peso closed marginally weaker at 26.285 to the dollar from Friday's 26.284 after the Central Bank supported the peso from sliding further by selling dollars in the market, brokers said.
"The peso moved within a tight range," one trader said. The peso was stuck between a low of 26.287 to a high of 26.280, which was the rate for trades settled the same day.
The Central Bank sold an estimated $22 million at 26.285 out of the $119.7 million traded in the market.
The fall in the local bourse earlier in the day did not affect the peso exchange rate as most of the trades in the stock exchange will be settled four days after.
The trader added that inflows into the debt market, especially in the long-termed Treasury bonds, kept the system afloat.
Demand of oil companies was weak with only $900 million which were done at an average of 26.2825 pesos per dollar.
The parallel rate was trading lower at 26.310 to the dollar.
